newsitem.title: UK: London gold, palladium fix firmer then edge back.
newsitem.headline: London gold, palladium fix firmer then edge back.

text.p: Palladium fixed at a new fresh high on Friday afternoon as market tightness pushed up prices but gold encountered selling when buyers tried to lift it out of its narrow range.
"As long as the Russia-Japan export problem contiues, palladium is not going to go down. Nobody wants to be short," one dealer said.
He was referring to the near five-month long delay in agreeing a supply contract between these two countries, the leading exporter and consumer of palladium respectively.
Palladium was fixed at $161.50 per ounce, up $2.50 from the morning and its highest fixing since May 31, 1995.
After the fixing it settled back to around $160 where the market has twice peaked in the past few weeks.
The tight supply was reflected in lease or borrowing rates standing at an unusually high 15 percent for one month.
"There may have been some stocks available (in Europe) earlier this year, but there is none around now," a dealer said.
The gold market struggled to get out of its $340.00-$342.50 range of the past week as it met resistance at the top end.
It fixed at $342.25 up from $341.35 at the morning setting and $340.90 on Thursday afternoon.
The Comex June contract was up $1.40 at $344.10 just under the resistance at $345.00 which had capped business so far this week.
Dealers said there was some buying against Monday's OTC option expiry at which most interest would be on the $340 call.
The weekend's G7 meeting in Washington provoked mildly mixed feelings for next week's direction.
Even just talking about the International Monetary Fund selling gold from reserves, which was a likely G7 discussion point, would be negative, one analyst said.
On foreign exchange discussions, the analyst added, "Any talk of reducing the strength of the dollar is likely to be hot air but it could be helpful for gold."
Platinum egded ahead helped by palladium to $378.50/$379.50 having touched $380.00 bid.
Like palladium supplies are tight and dealers nervous after a gap of around five months in supplies from Russia, the second largest exporter of the metal after South Africa.
Silver was about two cents firmer at $4.73/$4.75 and received some attention from option players defending the $4.70 call ahead of Monday's expiry.
